name: Pet sitter

pf.license.need: Usually none to visit or stay with pets at the owner's home. Boarding pets at the sitter's own home or a kennel is licensed in some states: where the state's rules require it, the form asks for the boarding license. Some cities ask for a business license.
pf.license.ask: The company's business registration. For boarding, the state's boarding or kennel license number, where the form asks for one.
pf.license.who_holds: The business. Sitters need no license of their own unless the state's form says so.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks_live: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.inspections: Where the state inspects boarding homes, a lapsed license or a failed inspection pauses boarding bookings (the license re-check).
pf.license.insurance_bond: Pet-care insurance or a bond is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
pf.license.background_checks: Only where the state's rules require them, or as the business's own word.
pf.license.not_this_work: Vet care (checking or treating a sick pet) is a vet's work. Grooming is its own kind of work.

pf.services.pattern: Set service: care visits or stays while the owner is away, priced per visit or per night. Boarding is a stay at the business.

pf.services.stays: A booking of several visits or nights is one booking: its first and last day, each visit inside it, one price, one $2.
pf.services.not_offered: Vet care and grooming. A pet with a bite history only if the owner OKs it after a meet-and-greet.

words: a pet hurt, not breathing, bleeding, having a seizure, or that ate something toxic, right now

what_happens: A pet in danger now: Rosie can't judge how sick a pet is. It says to call the vet or go to the nearest emergency vet now, gives the business's emergency vet line if the plug-in has one, and books nothing.
A bite history: the request goes to the owner first. The owner decides, after a meet-and-greet.
A gas smell or a fire: leave and call 911. No booking until it's safe.
A lost pet during care: the sitter texts LOST. The owner and the customer are told at once.
pf.safety.booking_goes_on: No, for a pet in danger now (the vet comes first). Only with the owner's OK for a bite history.

pf.first_steps.meet_and_greet: New clients get a free 30-minute meet-and-greet before the first booking. Pet sitting: at the customer's home, to meet the pets, see the food, medicine and litter, and take the key. Boarding: at the Lodge, where the dog meets the sitters and the other dogs. It stays good while the same sitter cares for the pets; a new sitter meets them first where there's time.
pf.first_steps.papers: A care sheet and the business's service agreement, signed on the secure page before the first visit: food, medicine, the vet, an emergency contact and the emergency vet OK with its spending limit.
pf.first_steps.vaccines: Boarding: vaccine records on file before the first night (rabies, and the others the business or the state's rules require). A vet's written exemption where the rules allow it. The vet can send them.
pf.first_steps.boarding_notice: Boarding at a home: any notice the state's rules require before booking, like overnight cover and time alone, signed on the secure page.
prep_for_reminder: Leave out food, litter and medicine supplies
Check the care sheet is current
Codes go on the secure page, never in a text
Boarding: bring the food, any medicine and the leash

pf.visit.check_in: Pet sitting: nobody's home, so there's no code. The sitter lets themself in with the key from the meet-and-greet, a lockbox or a door code. Each visit ends with a photo. DONE after the last visit closes the booking. Someone home (a meet-and-greet): the code at the door. Boarding: the code at drop-off.
pf.visit.pick_up: Boarding: a pet goes home only with its owner, who gives the code, or someone they named on the secure page, who shows an ID.
pf.visit.entry_codes: Shown only to the booked sitter, only on visit days, each view logged, deleted after the last visit. Keys are kept or returned, the customer's choice, on tags with no address.
pf.visit.lockout: The key or code fails with nobody home: the sitter texts it, the customer gets one link for a new code, and the sitter waits 30 minutes. Pets can't go without care, so the owner calls the customer and the emergency contact. A fee only if the owner confirms it.
pf.visit.updates: A photo and a short note after each visit: fed, water, litter, medicine given. Boarding: one a day, with a photo.
pf.visit.vet_plan: A pet unwell: the sitter calls the vet on file or takes the pet to the emergency vet, as the customer agreed on the secure page, up to their spending limit. The customer and the owner are told at once. The vet's bill is the customer's.
pf.visit.changes_at_visit: An extra visit, an extra night or a vet trip only when the customer says yes, with the price first.
pf.visit.proof_done: A photo at each visit; DONE after the last visit. Boarding: the pick-up with the code.

pf.money.start: Pet sitting: a card saved at booking for the late-cancel fee; the whole booking charged when the sitter texts DONE after the last visit. Boarding: a card saved for the late-cancel fee; paid at pick-up.
pf.money.other_ways: A bill texted after the last visit (nothing taken at booking); a deposit, or the full price, for holiday and long bookings.
pf.money.deposits: Within the state's caps (the example: a $40 deposit, or 25% on a special-care price). Deposit cap: from the state form.
pf.money.fees: Late cancel (the example: after 7am the day care starts): the business's own fee (the example: $89 for pet sitting; $20 for a night of boarding, $40 for 4 nights or more), never more than the booking. The owner confirms each one; no answer, no fee.
pf.money.vet_bills: Paid by the customer to the vet, never through Rosie.
pf.money.tips: Optional, all to the sitter. A tip line only if the owner turns it on; card tips follow the state's rules.
pf.money.tax: A sales tax line only where the state taxes pet care, from the state form.
pf.money.rosfield_fee: The usual $2 per confirmed booking: one $2 for a booking of several visits.

pf.messages.emergency_contact: Listed on the secure page. Rosie never texts them unless they agreed to texts; the sitter or the owner calls them.
pf.messages.minors: Nobody under 18 books. A teen at home isn't the booking's adult.

pf.staff.licenses: None per person unless the state's form says so.
pf.staff.new_person_ok: A sitter the customer hasn't met is offered by text first, never sent without an OK, and meets the pets first where there's time. Only a sitter with the skill (like insulin shots) is offered.
pf.staff.keys: Each key is on a tag with no address. A backup key only for a backup sitter the customer OK'd.
pf.staff.who_oks: The owner OKs holiday bookings and new clients with a bite history. The office manager may too; the owner's answer wins.

pf.rules.agreement: The business's service agreement and care sheet, signed on the secure page before the first visit.
pf.rules.vet_ok: The customer's signed OK for emergency vet care, with a spending limit.
pf.rules.boarding: Boarding at a home or a kennel: a license, inspections, vaccine records, the number of pets and any notice before booking, where the state's rules require them.
pf.rules.holiday: Holiday dates the owner sets: their own minimum nights, price, deposit and free-cancel cut-off, shown before booking.
pf.rules.keys_codes: Codes deleted after the last visit; keys kept or returned, the customer's choice (Rosie's rule).
pf.rules.records: 7 years, with the visit photos and the care sheet.

matter_most: A pet unwell or hurt during care: the vet plan the customer signed. The customer and the owner are told at once.
A lost pet: LOST from the sitter. The owner and the customer are told at once; the times are logged. Rosie never offers money.
The key or code fails with nobody home: one link for a new code; the sitter waits 30 minutes; the owner calls the customer and the emergency contact.
The sitter is out: a sitter with the skill is offered first, never sent without the customer's OK. No answer: the owner calls, since pets can't go without care.
The trip changes: days added or cut, priced first, with the customer's yes.
A meet-and-greet not done before the first visit: the owner decides. A full refund if the booking can't go ahead.
A pet not picked up from boarding: reminders; extra nights at the nightly price only after the customer is told.
Several open bookings (a meet-and-greet and the trip): which one is asked first.
pf.edges.rest: All other edge cases are handled the generic way.
